newsitem.title: USA: Pakistan may buy up to 250,000 T U.S. wheat -trade.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan may buy up to 250,000 T U.S. wheat -trade.

text.p: Pakistan may buy up to 250,000 tonnes of U.S. white wheat at a tender set for Monday, but limited GSM-102 credits may restrict the country from buying the full 500,000 tonnes it is seeking, export sources said.

"They just got $25 million in GSM credits this week but that only gets them about 150,000 to 175,000 tonnes," one exporter said. "They're going to buy white wheat which is at about $4 a bushel right now."
That would put the price per tonne near $146.80, FOB.
Pakistan is set to tender on Monday for 500,000 tonnes optional origin wheat, an Pakistan embassy source in Washington confirmed on Friday.

The U.S. Agriculture Department on Thursday said it raised by $25 million the amount of GSM-102 credit guarantees available for sales of U.S. farm goods to Pakistan under the Export Credit Guarantee Program.
The action increases Pakistan's fiscal year 1997 allocation to $325 million.
USDA has estimated Pakistan will buy three million tonnes of wheat during the 1997-98 (June/May) crop marketing year, but some trade sources have put the purchases closer to four million tonnes.
Canada and Australia also have wheat to sell, but exporters said Pakistan was unlikely to buy more than a total of 150,000 tonnes of wheat from those countries.
"I don't see Australia being real competitive," a second exporter said. "Canada might do 100,000 tonnes, so I don't know where else they're going to go."
"If there is an attractive price out of Canada, they may buy one to three cargoes," another exporter said. One cargo typically contains 50,000 tonnes.
Pakistan on Wednesday received $20 million in PL-480 food-for-peace credits, but export sources said they must tender separately to use those credits and cannot apply them to Monday's tender.
"They're going to have to jump through too many hoops to get the PL-480 money this time around," another exporter said. "They might not buy the full 500,000 and then tender for the PL-480 later."
At current prices, Pakistan could buy roughly 135,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat with the $20 million in PL-480 funds.
